title: Subways
objective: After this level you can explain how subways changed cities.
summary: London's Metropolitan Railway (1863) ran steam trains through cut-and-cover trenches; electric deep tubes followed in 1890. The railway then sold 'Metro-land' and built suburbs for its commuters.

cards.headline: In 1863, Londoners rode steam trains under the streets.
cards.body: The world's first underground railway, London's Metropolitan Railway, opened on 10 January 1863, hauled by steam locomotives. Picture a smoky train in a tunnel. How did they build it, and what did it do to the city above?

cards.headline: Dig up the street, then put it back
cards.body: The Metropolitan was built by cut and cover. Workers dug trenches along the streets, gave them brick sides, and roofed them over with iron girders or a brick arch. Then the street went back on top. It's the way you'd bury a garden hose: dig a trench, lay it in, cover it up. Just with a train, and a very inconvenienced London.

cards.headline: Deeper, and electric
cards.body: Cut and cover meant digging up whole streets. In 1890 London opened the first electric underground railway, the first deep "tube," dug by tunnelling instead of trenching. A deep tunnel runs far below the streets instead of in a trench just under them, so the street above can stay put.

cards.fact: A railway that grew its own passengers.
cards.context: In 1915 the Metropolitan Railway began selling the countryside along its line as "Metro-land," a place for commuters to live. From 1919, a company it set up built housing estates on spare land the railway owned. The trains didn't just serve the suburbs; they created them. Build the line, then build the homes that fill the trains.

mascot.line: Hold on to this: in the next level, suburbs keep following the ride.

cards.headline: Subways: running
learned: Cut and cover: trench, brick sides, roof, street back on
Metro-land: the railway built its own suburbs

questions.prompt: When London's Metropolitan Railway opened in 1863, its trains were powered by _____.

options.label: horses
options.rationale: It was a railway with locomotives.

questions.explanation: The Metropolitan Railway opened on 10 January 1863 with steam locomotives.

questions.prompt: Put these steps in London's underground story in order, from earliest to latest.
questions.explanation: Steam trains ran under the streets from 1863. The first electric underground railway opened in 1890. The Metropolitan began selling "Metro-land" in 1915, and from 1919 it built housing estates.

questions.prompt: Some Metropolitan Railway trenches were roofed with a brick arch. As Level 4 explained, how does an arch carry the street above?

options.label: Its bricks are stretched, so it works in tension
options.rationale: An arch keeps its blocks in compression.

options.label: Weight squeezes its wedge-shaped blocks together
Steel bars hidden inside take all of the load
options.rationale: A brick arch needs no steel.

options.label: The trains below push it upward and hold it up
options.rationale: The arch carries weight down, not the train.

questions.explanation: Weight pressing down forces an arch's wedge-shaped blocks together, keeping them in compression, so a brick arch can carry a street.
